podcast.body: This self-titled debut LP was released by the Deram label in 1967, but it ultimately failed to make the charts. It was issued after Bowie had found his name and voice but before he had found his distinctive sound or image, leading to him being dropped by the label in 1968. "Neither the single nor the self-titled David Bowie album made the charts."

podcast.body: This self-titled album, released in 1969, was Bowie's second, although marketed as if his flop 1967 LP had never happened. It was rushed by Mercury Records to capitalize on the Apollo 11 moon landing. Later, RCA repackaged this LP as 'Space Oddity, the album', adding a newer Ziggy-era photo on the cover, which helped it break into the top 20 on the album chart in 1973. "After Bowie signed to Major Label Mercury Records, they rushed release the single to capitalize on that summer's excitement over the Apollo 11 moon landing, as well as a second self-titled David Bowie album, as if his flop 1967 LP had never happened."
